summary: TM-16's 'consider signing the router source archive' (ADR-0139, proposed). CI change only, router and agent unchanged. .github/workflows/release-provenance.yml gets a second job router-source with its own job-level permissions (contents: write to upload the asset, id-token: write and attestations: write to sign) and the workflow-level permissions: {} unchanged. It runs on release published or workflow_dispatch with a tag, checks out the tag with persist-credentials: false, reads the router version from common.py and refuses anything but digits and dots (no injection into the file name), writes skirnir-router-<version>.tar.gz with git archive of router/ at HEAD, attests it with actions/attest-build-provenance at the commit already pinned in the same file (ADR-0055), and uploads it with gh release upload --clobber. No secret is used beyond github.token; no attacker-controlled input reaches a shell except the tag, which is passed through env and only used as an argument (as in the existing job). Independent of the agent rebuild job. This rules/CI change is flagged for maintainer review: its first real run is the next release.

tests.command: local: git archive --format=tar.gz --prefix=skirnir-router-<v>/ HEAD router; extract; check files
tests.evidence: the archive (0.42.14 at the time, 719 kB) holds every file install.sh requires in router/ (router.py, skirnir_router/, unit, layout script, minimal config, requirements and lock, ui.html/js/css, install.sh).

tests.command: python -c yaml.safe_load(release-provenance.yml); python test/check_pinned_references.py; python test/selftest_pinned_references.py
tests.evidence: two jobs parse; 0 pin findings; pin self-test 0 failures.

tests.command: every python test/... and tools/... command of all workflows in .github/workflows/, except run_tests.py and check_public_changes; plus ruff check .

limitations: The release workflow cannot run before a release is published; its first real run is the next release (or a manual run with an existing tag).
The attestation proves the archive came from the workflow at that tag, not a reproducible rebuild of its bytes.
Extending the agent rebuild to releases whose agent came from an earlier commit (TM-16's other item) is not part of this change.
